title: Microsoft Entra ID: passkey support for B2B guest users
summary: Hold: the authentication-strength API creates a custom strength but does not make guests use passkeys to access a resource, as its control row claims. The roadmap facts and licensing statements are supported, and the briefing correctly distinguishes Microsoft's plan from Learn's current guest-registration restrictions.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Passkey user/group targeting and profile assignment are reached through Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies > Passkey (FIDO2) > Enable and Target.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies. Select Passkey (FIDO2). Select Enable and Target. Select Add target, and then choose All users or Select targets to choose specific groups.
claims.fix: The route reaches the correct tab but stops before profile assignment. Extend it to 'Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies > Passkey (FIDO2) > Enable and Target > Add target > target > passkey profiles', using the cited page. State that passkey profiles must first be enabled through the banner opt-in link if the tenant has not enabled them.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/fido2 updates the tenant's passkey targeting and profiles.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/fido2; "includeTargets"; "allowedPasskeyProfiles"; "excludeTargets"; "passkeyProfiles"
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to controls[0].note: 'The request body uses includeTargets and excludeTargets for targeting, includeTargets[].allowedPasskeyProfiles for profile assignment, and passkeyProfiles for profile configuration.' These properties appear in the cited v1.0 update example.

claims.claim: Authentication Policy Administrator is the least privileged role for the FIDO2 configuration update.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role ... Authentication Policy Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.

claims.claim: Entra ID > Authentication methods > Registration campaign reaches the campaign configuration page.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Authentication methods > Registration campaign, and select Edit. For State: Select Enabled to enable and configure the registration campaign.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Entra ID > Authentication methods > Registration campaign > Edit > State > Enabled > Authentication method > Passkey'. Add to the note: 'Select included or excluded users and groups on this page.' The cited page gives these remaining steps.

claims.where: controls[1].api and note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/authenticationmethodspolicy with the updated registrationEnforcement section configures a passkey campaign and its include/exclude targets.
claims.quote: To update the policy, perform a PATCH on the authentication methods policy with only the updated registrationEnforcement section: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authenticationmethodspolicy

claims.claim: Entra ID > Authentication methods > Authentication strengths > New authentication strength reaches custom-strength creation.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Authentication methods > Authentication strengths. Select New authentication strength. Provide a Name for your new authentication strength. ... Select Passkeys (FIDO2).
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Entra ID > Authentication methods > Authentication strengths > New authentication strength > Passkeys (FIDO2)', as given on the cited page. This selects the method in a custom strength; it does not apply a Conditional Access policy.

claims.where: controls[2].api and governs; Governance controls table and following paragraph
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/policies/authenticationStrengthPolicies implements the row's control over whether guests must use passkeys to reach a resource.
claims.quote: Create a new custom authenticationStrengthPolicy object. POST /policies/authenticationStrengthPolicies. allowedCombinations: The authentication method combinations allowed by this authentication strength policy.
claims.fix: Keep the documented call, but narrow controls[2].governs and its table label to 'Which authentication methods a custom authentication strength permits'. Set its note to 'The request body sets allowedCombinations to ["fido2"]. Creates a custom strength only; a Conditional Access policy must apply it. Applies to external users who authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID.' Replace 'The first three are rows above' with 'The Authentication methods policy and registration campaign are rows above; the third row creates an authentication strength, not a Conditional Access policy.'
